## About Me

I'm a Senior Data Scientist with over a decade of experience building analytics and machine learning systems that support real business decisions. My work has spanned retail analytics, manufacturing R&D, and applied scientific computing, giving me the opportunity to solve problems ranging from customer recommendation systems to experimental design and physical modeling.

I'm currently available for remote roles and am based in Phoenix, AZ. Feel free to reach out to me over [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nick-gould/).

## What I Work On

Much of my professional work has centered on building end-to-end data products rather than isolated models. That includes

* designing data pipelines
* developing machine learning models
* deploying and monitoring production systems
* building experimentation frameworks
* creating dashboards and decision-support tools

I've worked extensively with Python, SQL, Databricks, Snowflake, and modern data engineering workflows, with an emphasis on reproducibility, maintainability, and long-term reliability.

Beyond machine learning, I enjoy applying statistical thinking to practical problems. Designing experiments, quantifying uncertainty, and translating technical analyses into actionable recommendations have been recurring themes throughout my career.

## How I Work

One lesson I've learned over the years is that successful data science projects rarely fail because of the model—they fail because the wrong problem was solved, the results weren't trusted, or the solution didn't fit into existing workflows.

For that reason, I spend as much time understanding the problem as I do choosing algorithms. I prefer simple models that answer the right question over sophisticated models that solve the wrong one. I also believe that reproducibility, documentation, and clear communication are as important as predictive performance when building systems that people depend on.

I enjoy working across disciplines, collaborating with engineers, researchers, product teams, and business stakeholders to build solutions that balance technical rigor with practical constraints.


## About _This_ Project

Most of the projects I've worked on professionally are proprietary, making it difficult to share the technical details that don't fit on a resume. This site is my way of recreating the kinds of problems I've solved throughout my career while demonstrating how I think about modeling, experimentation, visualization, and software engineering.

The intention is twofold:

* Bridge the gap from the resume to the conversation. A typical hiring manager looks at a resume for a single-digit number of seconds, and the commitment from looking at a resume to scheduling a call is high; going from seconds to a half-hour or hour. This site can be navigated in minutes with hopefully enough depth where you can verify the things on my resume are true and that I'm worth talking to.
* These subjects often come up in conversations at work, conferences, or parties (I have _that_ kind of friends group). Having something to share with them will be nice.

This project will be iterative, with mildly ambitious plans for different topics. Instead of letting the perfect be the enemy of the good it will be ~~git add . && git commit -m "perfect website, no notes" && git push -u origin main~~ published piecemeal.

Many of the pages include interactive simulations and notebooks built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/), allowing readers to explore concepts rather than simply read about them. The site itself also serves as a demonstration of reproducible technical workflows using Git, GitHub Pages, and modern Python tooling.

## Select Projects

### [Design of Experiments](posts/DesignOfExperiments.html)

Design of Experiments (DoE) is a collection of methods that intends to use statistics to systematically vary possible causes that affect a given output to better understand, control, and optimize the system being investigated. A well designed DoE can often turn months worth of work into a couple of days.

### [Lorenz Attractor Simulator](https://nick-gould.github.io/Lorenz-Simulator/){target="_blank"}

A dashboard-style Lorenz attractor simulator that runs entirely client-side; Python via [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org/en/stable/) (WebAssembly) for the computation, [Plotly](https://plotly.com/python/) for the 3D visualization, no server involved. Built to test whether "static site with real interactivity" is a viable pattern for shipping data tools without backend overhead. It is.
